item.title: Digest for 2026-10-30
item.description:
Your stack

Linters and type checkers

ty 0.0.95 and semgrep 1.183.0 shipped; no changelog notes.

pydantic

pydantic 2.14.2 and a matching 1.10.27 backport landed; no changelog detail.

boto3

boto3 1.43.122 is out, again with no changelog.

AWS Lambda

BMW Group moved its connected-vehicle platform to AWS Graviton, cutting ingress CPU ~57% and improving price-performance ~40% with Karpenter and multi-arch builds.

Step Functions

Step Functions workflows can now be exposed as AI agent tools through Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, letting an agent decide when to invoke a workflow.

DynamoDB

DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) expanded to Canada (Central) and Africa (Cape Town).

EventBridge

A guide to full-stack Outposts observability leans on EventBridge with Systems Manager and CloudWatch for unified visibility.

Amazon Bedrock

boAt built its AI Coach feature on Bedrock and Lambda for real-time fitness coaching at scale. Epsilon built a managed UI-testing service on Nova Act and the AgentCore Browser Tool, with tests written in plain English. MoEngage turned ~400 private REST APIs into agent tools via AgentCore Gateway, replacing per-service MCP servers. AWS Agent Registry (AgentCore) expanded to four more regions.

Dependabot and supply chain

GitHub previewed an npm firewall that inspects package metadata and downloads for malicious activity before install.

Checkmarx

Checkmarx's write-up on the chaotic PHP patch response argues most orgs lack a real remediation plan for critical vulnerabilities, via one CTO's 48-hour scramble.

MCP

Ben Hylak, quoted by Simon Willison, needles the "every product should just be a headless MCP" agent-everything pitch.

Claude

Claude Platform shipped a beta Usage and Cost Analytics API and raised the Messages/Token-Counting request-size cap to 128MB. The Claude Agent SDK hit 0.2.175. Claude Haiku 5.5 is now on Bedrock via Canada cross-Region inference for data-residency needs. OpenAI matched Anthropic's API-credits benefit with an equivalent ChatGPT offer. Simon Willison also flags a writeup on a multiplayer game world run by autonomous Fable-class agents.

Claude Code

Claude Code 2.1.314 adds a permission that blocks writes outside the working directory in every permission mode, plus IdP-group routing for Claude apps gateway upstreams.

AI-DLC and AI-assisted development practices

AWS shows how to turn a PHP-to-Java migration into a repeatable Kiro-driven engine with a parity harness. GitHub made plugin defaults and enterprise plugin controls for Copilot CLI, VS Code and the Copilot app GA. Martin Fowler's team explores why experienced developers stay wary of agentic development: built isn't the same as working in production.

Security (AI and cloud)

Google's Gemini 4 Carbon tops vulnerability-finding benchmarks, leading SEC-bench Pro at 88.2%. Anthropic disclosed that its own model wrote a working exploit for a 9.8-CVSS Linux kernel TCP flaw hitting Ubuntu and RHEL. Attackers are impersonating ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps to plant crypto miners via fake GitHub projects (campaign "Yoba"). A researcher found 26,400 working cloud and AI credentials exposed across public Gitee repos. Hacker News also covers how AI is reshaping SOC roles, and Wiz catalogs what agentic attacks look like in the wild. AWS disclosed CVE-2026-119115, an authorization flaw letting a namespace-scoped approver in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes obtain certificates beyond scope.

Python

  • Real Python launched "Mentor AI," a conversational way to work through async Python topics.
  • The PSF announced its 2026 Community Service Award recipients.

JavaScript and TypeScript

  • Node shipped security releases fixing a Brotli decoder flaw (see Datadog below); Node 26 "Lithium" is now the active LTS line through April 2029.

Rust

  • A community member shared Crossfyre, five security-scanning engines in one open-source Rust workspace (Apache-2.0).
  • Another shared Automock, a new crate for mocking functions, traits and structs.

Java

  • JDK 27 has shipped; Inside Java runs through what changed in the G1, Parallel and Serial collectors.
  • Eight compromised eMudhra CA certificates affect some OpenJDK runtimes; Inside Java has mitigation steps.

Source control and GitHub

  • GitHub added new webhook IP ranges to the Meta API — worth a check if you maintain a static network allowlist.

AWS

  • Aurora PostgreSQL now supports post-quantum TLS key exchange for data in transit.
  • SageMaker AI training jobs now start in seconds with SOCI-indexed images, cutting GPU idle time up to 90%.
  • NVIDIA's 120B-parameter Nemotron 3.5 Super VL model gets a deployment guide for EKS and SageMaker HyperPod.

AI and agents

  • Latent Space's Elorian benchmark probes whether frontier models reason past visual decoys, not just see them.

Security

  • Cisco patched an actively-exploited ASA/FTD VPN flaw (CVSS 8.6) that can crash firewalls.
  • Cisco Talos found "KeyDrift" malware planted via a patched Catalyst SD-WAN flaw, built to steal site-to-site encryption keys.
  • Binance disclosed a breach affecting $6.3 billion in assets, nearly $3 billion frozen on-chain so far.
  • Datadog reproduced CVE-2026-111497, the out-of-bounds write in Node's bundled Brotli decoder, with remediation steps.
  • Wiz's follow-up on PHP2Shell exploitation says attempts continue but none have succeeded yet.
  • An attacker tried exploiting a CVSS-10.0 GitLab flaw on Alpine Linux's own server a week after the fix shipped; no compromise found.

AI security

  • Daniel Miessler sketches "General Hill-Climbing," a five-stage loop from defining an ideal state through evals to iterating.

Engineering practice

  • The Pragmatic Engineer talks with Titus Winters about engineering at Google's scale and AI's effect on CS education.
  • Martin Fowler's bliki names the "LLM voice" that makes writing feel machine-generated.

Feeds that failed

  • Microsoft Teams Blog (what's new) (https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/s/gxcuf89792/rss/board?board.id=MicrosoftTeamsBlog): malformed response (not well-formed XML)
  • CISA advisories (https://www.cisa.gov/cybersecurity-advisories/all.xml): HTTP 403 Forbidden

item.title: Digest for 2026-10-29
item.description:
Your stack

Linters and type checkers

checkov 3.4.0, mypy 2.4.1, and ty 0.0.94 all shipped; no changelog notes in any feed.

Powertools for AWS Lambda

Powertools for AWS Lambda (Python) 3.38.0 is out, again with no changelog detail.

AWS Lambda

Lambda Managed Instances now support Seekable OCI (SOCI) for lazy-loading container images, cutting container startup by up to 70%. Durable functions gained a telemetry exporter emitting one record per execution to 13 destinations, with a companion MCP server for querying that history.

API Gateway

A case study on how Revinate built its guest-engagement APIs on API Gateway, a useful reference architecture for API-first products.

Amazon Bedrock

AgentCore CLI hit GA at version 1.0, with faster startup and a more consistent command structure. A companion post covers a reference architecture for a governed, multi-account AgentCore platform with CI/CD gating per agent.

GitHub Actions

GitHub Agentic Workflows is now GA for automating issue triage and CI-failure analysis as workflow files. Actions also got multi-cloud compute for hosted runners and GA dependency lockfiles. Wiz, meanwhile, audited what pwn-request attacks still work post-pull_request_target changes, and found a campaign planting secret-dumping workflows via stolen tokens.

GitHub Enterprise

GitHub Enterprise now bundles Copilot access for every licensed user under a GitHub/Microsoft account team.

MCP

Real Python has a tutorial on building a minimal MCP client in Python over stdio, for testing your own MCP servers from the terminal.

Claude

Latent Space has a long interview on how Anthropic ships the Claude Platform, covering Opus 5.5 and keeping the "brain" separate from the agent's "hands". Elsewhere: Anthropic is reportedly dropping coding interviews and filed an S-1 for a $2T IPO; and an unreleased Anthropic model chained flaws into working browser/OS exploits (Chrome, Safari, Windows, Linux), all patched pre-disclosure.

AI-DLC and AI-assisted development practices

GitHub Universe brought a wave of Copilot changes: Copilot Fusion (model routing) went GA and now routes to local, on-device models; a new security extension surfaces code-scanning alerts inside the Copilot app; and teams can share Copilot Automations. Also: Simon Willison argues October 2026 is an inflection point for vibe-coded games, and Latent Space covers running a fully offline coding agent with OpenCode, Ollama and Qwen.

Entra ID

Wiz is tracking an AI agent-driven actor (Storm-0940) attacking Okta, Entra ID and Cognito across software vendors.

Security (AI and cloud)

Three new AWS Security Bulletins: unverified Athena query-result ownership in AWS SDK for pandas (CVE-2026-118029), a secret-masking bypass in Strands Agents Tools via a crafted prompt (CVE-2026-115415), and RCE and memory disclosure in the native Brotli decoder, affecting Lambda, Amplify, App Runner and others (CVE-2026-111497).

React

  • Next.js now ships a bundle-optimizer agent skill plus new Bundle Analyzer tooling to shrink your shipped JavaScript.

Java

  • OpenJDK published an overview of its Secure Coding Guidelines, with examples of insecure patterns and updates covering input validation and serialization.
  • Spring AI 2.1 adds "message parts" so reasoning-model thinking blocks survive a round trip intact.
  • Spring AI 2.1 also adds upsert for pre-computed embeddings, for apps that generate their own vectors.

Source control and GitHub

  • GitHub Universe 2026 laid out GitHub's vision as an end-to-end software delivery system.
  • This year's Octoverse report shows commits and pushes at record highs as more development work runs through agents.
  • A new "GitHub intelligence" feature feeds team conventions and history into Copilot so agents follow your team's own practices, not just the code.

Microsoft (Azure DevOps, Teams, WSL)

  • SharePoint Embedded gets a streamlined path for AI-ready custom apps that pull in Microsoft 365 content without a full site.
  • Copilot UX components are GA with SPFx 1.24, for embedding interactive dashboards and forms directly in Microsoft Copilot.

AWS

  • IAM Identity Center's Identity Store now streams change events to EventBridge when users, groups or memberships change.
  • Nubank's case study on automating disaster recovery with the AWS DevOps Agent across thousands of EKS microservices.
  • Smarsh encoded the AWS Agentic AI Well-Architected Lens as a Claude skill to review an agentic workload against all 150 best practices in hours.
  • Part 3 of AWS's agentic QA automation series with Nova Act adds test organization and team-based ownership controls.
  • Amazon Quick added "smart approvals" to cut approval-prompt fatigue on agentic actions.

AI and agents

  • Google's Gemini 4 Carbon tops independent evals, launching first for cyber-defense teams.
  • A Latent Space interview on why agent builders are reaching for Supabase as backend infrastructure.

Security

  • New research shows AI models can provably hide arbitrary capabilities from evaluators under adversarial conditions.
  • Tailscale patched SSH forwarding flaws (fixed in 1.104.4) that could let a compromised device reach root-only services on other nodes.
  • A 16-year-old flaw in the EDK II UEFI firmware code used by most hardware makers can run code before Secure Boot on network-booting servers.
  • A China-nexus actor exploited a VMware ESX zero-day to scrub audit trails; CISA has added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
  • PHP patched two critical unauthenticated RCEs in its request lifecycle; upgrade or apply the vendor backport if you're on an older release.
  • Volt Typhoon's covert "Silent Train" access network has been used in four separate zero-day campaigns via compromised SOHO and IoT devices.

Engineering practice

  • Martin Fowler's latest Fragments covers Andrej Karpathy's view of a widening gap between how the public and AI-forward professionals perceive LLM capability.

Feeds that failed

  • CISA advisories (https://www.cisa.gov/cybersecurity-advisories/all.xml): HTTP 403 Forbidden

item.title: Digest for 2026-10-28
item.description:
Your stack

  • uv: tar-codec, Astral's new Rust tar encoder/decoder, is now uv's default and more than doubles its tar-handling speed while hardening against archive differentials.
  • Linters and type checkers: Real Python published a walkthrough of Pyrefly, Meta's fast Rust-based type checker, covering catching type errors, generating annotations and measuring coverage; separately, ty 0.0.93 is a routine patch release of Astral's type checker.
  • pytest: pytest 9.2.0 is out.
  • boto3: boto3 1.43.120 ships the usual batch of updated AWS service models.
  • Amazon Bedrock: AWS shows how to build document-investigation agents where an AWS Lambda function and a Bedrock AgentCore agent share an Amazon S3 Files file system using ordinary file operations instead of upload/download code; separately, a Bedrock customer writeup on fixing evaluation bias found 96.8% of their vision-AI eval labels were inherited from the incumbent model, masking its true accuracy — worth a look if you lean on model evals.
  • Azure DevOps: the Azure DevOps Server RC (26H2) is available, bringing previously hosted-only features plus security and quality fixes on-prem.
  • MCP: Real Python's MCP vs. API calls piece builds one Python tool both ways and compares what each approach costs and when an MCP server actually pays for itself.
  • Claude Code: 2.1.312 adds an effort-level picker for cloud routines, an oidc.user_id_claim option so the apps gateway can identify people by a claim other than sub (handy for Microsoft Entra ID's oid), and fixes subagent/prompt hooks running more than their intended 24-at-a-time limit.
  • AI-DLC and AI-assisted development practices: Real Python's overview of AI coding agent workflows breaks them into IDE, terminal, PR and cloud types and how each fits modern Python development; GitHub Copilot now supports server-to-server authentication for GitHub Apps on organizations (public preview), letting Copilot SDK-built services and agents make requests without a human in the loop; and AWS walks through using Kiro to build a SCORM pipeline that converts raw training material into LMS-ready packages.
  • Security (AI and cloud): Apple backported a fix for CVE-2026-86950, an actively-exploited CoreGraphics out-of-bounds write (CVSS 8.8), to older iPhones and iPads; Microsoft fixed CVE-2026-80097 in Authenticator for Android, where a permissionless malicious app could impersonate a trusted app like Teams and steal work-account sign-in tokens; and Node.js v24.22.1 and v22.23.4 are security releases fixing ten CVEs, including a Brotli-decoder flaw ("node2shell") that can lead to remote code execution.

Python

  • PEP 851 proposes list.discard(x), a non-raising counterpart to list.remove(), analogous to set.discard().
  • Real Python on Python circular imports: why they happen and how to fix them.

JavaScript and TypeScript

  • Buried in this week's JavaScript Weekly: TanStack AI reaches 1.0, a vendor-neutral AI toolkit with 23 provider adapters and a new long-running agent harness.

React

  • Next.js is preparing a scheduled security release for November 3.

Rust

  • Inside Rust shared results from its variadic generics survey, drawn from over 3,300 responses on a hypothetical language feature.
  • A Rust forum post on proptest's "residual risk" explains what a passing property-test run does, and doesn't, tell you.

Java

  • Inside Java flagged JDK 28's Value Classes for community quality testing ahead of release.

AWS

  • Amazon ECS now supports GPU sharing via NVIDIA MPS, letting multiple tasks share one GPU for small-model inference and similar partial-capacity workloads.
  • SageMaker MLflow Apps now support MLflow 3.16, with a redesigned trace explorer for debugging GenAI and ML workflows.
  • SOCI-indexed images take full container-image download off the critical path for SageMaker AI jobs, starting containers in seconds instead of minutes.
  • ElastiCache for Valkey now lets you change durability on existing node-based clusters in place, without a new cluster.
  • Anchorage Digital and Turnkey built verifiable infrastructure on AWS Nitro Enclaves so crypto wallets can cryptographically attest which code parsed a transaction.
  • Amazon ECR now supports replication backfill, so existing images can be replicated to new destinations without manual retagging.

AI and agents

  • Simon Willison on running a Game Boy/NES emulator on a conference badge, built with Gemini's help — a fun demo of AI-assisted hardware hacking at GitHub Universe.

Security

  • Route 53 Resolved IP Validation for AWS Network Firewall closes a gap where non-HTTP(S) protocols could bypass domain-based firewall rules via DNS tricks.
  • Google Project Zero compares Fuzzilli and BigSleep on V8: over six months, the LLM-based bug finder found more vulnerabilities than the generative fuzzer, with roughly 60% overlap.
  • OpenAI's conversation-compaction feature could be abused to leak a reasoning model's hidden chain-of-thought in plain text.
  • CyberStrikeAI used 44 AI agents to help automate three cyberattacks against organizations in Japan.
  • GoAhead's embedded web server loaded a certificate revocation list but never enabled revocation checking, letting revoked client certs still pass mutual-TLS logins.
  • AWS became the first CSP to complete the Cloud High (PBHH) security assessment, covering 172 services and features.

Engineering practice

  • The Pragmatic Engineer asks whether "AI SRE" actually works for on-call, beyond the vendor demos.

Feeds that failed

CISA advisories, Latent Space, Microsoft Teams Blog (what's new), OWASP GenAI Security Project, Schneier on Security, Simon Willison: prompt injection tag, fasterthanlime.

item.title: Digest for 2026-10-27
item.description:
Your stack

  • uv: 0.13.6 is a routine point release of Astral's package manager; Real Python also published a full walkthrough of managing projects with uv, a good reference to point teammates at.
  • ruff: 0.17.3 is a routine patch release of the Rust-based linter and formatter.
  • boto3: 1.43.119 ships the usual batch of updated AWS service models.
  • AWS Organizations and Control Tower: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports cross-Region trusted identity propagation, so permission sets issued in one Region can be trusted in another without re-provisioning.
  • Amazon Bedrock: GPT-6.1 Terra is now generally available on Bedrock, giving it a frontier OpenAI model alongside Claude and Nova; AWS also posted prompt-caching patterns for OpenAI models on Bedrock and a guide to agentic retrieval on a Bedrock Knowledge Base with CDK.
  • Terraform: AWS DevOps Agent can now trace failures across Terraform state boundaries, which should speed up debugging cross-module apply failures.
  • Azure DevOps: Microsoft posted guidance on what to check in Azure DevOps pipelines for exposure to the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities.
  • Microsoft Teams: Attackers are running Teams "IT support" scams to deploy malware and ransomware, worth a pass over your helpdesk-impersonation defenses.
  • GitHub Actions: Stolen GitHub tokens are being used to steal secrets printed into Actions logs; separately, Wiz's Pwn Request Reckoning finds classic pull_request_target-style attacks still work against many repos.
  • AI-DLC and AI-assisted development practices: Malware is being staged as a file an AI coding agent might "helpfully" install — treat agent-suggested installs from scanned files as untrusted. GitHub Copilot's assisted permissions feature is now GA, and Copilot picked up GPT-6.1 Terra as a selectable backend.
  • Claude: Anthropic posted its October 23 platform release notes, worth a skim for anything touching your Bedrock-hosted Claude usage.
  • Claude Code: 2.1.311 is a routine point release of the CLI.

Python

  • Build Command-Line Interfaces With Python's argparse — A practical argparse walkthrough for CLI tools.

  • ChromaDB: Embeddings and Vector Databases in Python — An intro to embeddings-backed search with ChromaDB.

Rust

  • How to fund Rust contributors — The Rust project's post on funding core contributors.

Go

  • Our Response To The eMudhra Key Disclosure Incident — The Go team's postmortem on a code-signing key disclosure affecting toolchain releases.

Java

  • Java News Roundup: JDK 28 Schedule, Oracle CPUs, eMudhra Certs, Apache POI, WildFly, Azul, BellSoft — InfoQ's roundup of JDK 28 planning and the same eMudhra certificate issue rippling across ecosystems.

AWS

  • AWS Key Management Service now supports ML-KEM for post-quantum key encapsulation — Adds a NIST post-quantum algorithm to KMS.
  • AWS EC2 Auto Scaling now supports Launch Before Terminate at account-level to replace instances — Auto Scaling can now provision replacements before terminating old instances, account-wide.
  • Recommended resilience testing in the next generation of AWS Resilience Hub — Updated guidance on resilience testing patterns.
  • The New York Times cut Oracle migration time from 18 to 5 months — A case study on accelerating a database migration off Oracle.
  • Data governance with annotations in Amazon S3 — A pattern for attaching governance metadata directly to S3 objects.

AI and agents

  • GPT-6.1 Terra — Simon Willison's first-look notes on OpenAI's new GPT-6.1 Terra model.
  • webframe: evaluated as a scraper and a sandbox — Willison evaluates a tool for safely scraping and sandboxing web content.

Security

  • CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Two PHP2Shell Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution — Patch urgently if you run affected PHP tooling; exploitation is already underway.
  • Two Critical Wasmtime Flaws Could Let Malicious WebAssembly Modules Escape Sandboxes — Relevant if you run untrusted Wasm, including some MCP or plugin sandboxes.
  • Microsoft 365 Token-Replay Attacks Compromise 97 Accounts at 79 Organizations — A token-replay campaign bypassed MFA at scale across dozens of organizations.
  • PHP Issues Second Windows Security Update in Five Days to Fix Brotli Code Execution Flaw — A second emergency patch in the same week, for a Brotli-related RCE bug.
  • Hackers Infect 953 Online Stores With Scanner-Evading JavaScript, Mostly on Magento — A large e-commerce skimmer campaign that evades automated scanners.

Feeds that failed

  • Microsoft Teams Blog (what's new) — feed returned malformed XML
  • CISA advisories — HTTP 403 Forbidden

item.title: Digest for 2026-10-26
item.description:
Your stack

  • Python 3.14: Python 3.15.2, 3.14.10, 3.13.18, 3.12.16 and 3.11.18 shipped as expedited security releases across every maintained line, purely to distrust the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys.
  • Linters and type checkers: ty 0.0.92 is out, Astral's latest point release of its Rust-based type checker.
  • FastAPI: FastAPI 0.162.0 released, the latest in its steady stream of point bumps.
  • Amazon Bedrock: Bedrock's Web Search tool now supports domain filtering and user-location controls, both configured on the existing web_search tool parameters. AWS also published a hands-on guide to multi-turn reinforcement learning on SageMaker AI that deploys the agent and reward model on Bedrock AgentCore, and a case study of Bayer Crop Science's agentic decision engine built the same way.
  • GitHub Enterprise: GitHub disclosed an EMU deletions bug — for two weeks in June, some Enterprise Managed User accounts deprovisioned via SCIM were deleted outright instead of being suspended and obfuscated as intended.
  • Microsoft Teams: a new GitHub app for Teams pairs notifications with Copilot, so a team can turn a flagged issue into a fix without leaving the channel.
  • MCP: AWS disclosed CVE-2026-115845, incomplete validation in the Python sandbox behind AWS MCP Server's run_script tool.
  • Claude: Anthropic's Python SDK bumped twice, to 2.2.0 and 2.3.0. The October 20 platform release notes (just surfaced) show the Claude Tag API reaching beta for Enterprise orgs, letting admins read and change Claude Tag settings on Slack channels via the API.
  • Claude Code: 2.1.310 adds the Monitor tool and plugin monitors on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry, moves cloud-session and Remote Control permissions under Enterprise custom roles, and clarifies the error an agent sees when an MCP tool call times out mid-elicitation. The Claude Agent SDK (Python) ticked to 0.2.174.
  • AI-DLC and AI-assisted development practices: AWS's open-source team introduced Infinity, a runtime built for coding agents that spend most of their time blocked on a long build or waiting hours for the next pull request.
  • Security (AI and cloud): AWS disclosed CVE-2026-111943 — a key-generation flaw let eMudhra/emSign intermediate CA private keys be recovered, exposing soft-fail TLS clients, including ALB OIDC/JWT auth, to man-in-the-middle risk, so AWS is pulling the roots from its trust bundles. A Brotli decoder memory-corruption flaw (CVE-2026-111497) reaches past Node.js into the Python brotli and brotlicffi packages and Bun. A critical Pillow flaw (CVE-2026-112900) lets a crafted EPS image run arbitrary OS commands via its Ghostscript handoff. And the Real Python podcast talks supply-chain defense with the PSF's security developer-in-residence, Seth Larson.

Python

  • PEP 813, the Pretty Print Protocol, got a second round of updates and looks ready to propose for Python 3.16.
  • Python's asyncio: A Hands-On Walkthrough — a practical tour of coroutines and awaitables.
  • Python Code Quality: Best Practices and Tools — what keeps a codebase healthy as it grows.

React

  • TanStack Start reached 1.0 after a year as a release candidate.

Go

  • Why Go had to hardcode a block on broken certs — the same eMudhra CA story, from Go's side.

Java

  • JEP 544 (Ahead-of-Time Code Compilation) is now targeted for JDK 28.
  • Pooled confined arenas make short-lived off-heap allocation 6–18x faster in JDK 28.
  • Spring shipped Spring AI 2.1.0-RC1 and Spring Boot 4.2.0-RC1.

Source control and GitHub

  • Public monitoring adds triage, validity checks, an API and webhooks for managing leaked-secret alerts at scale.
  • Enterprise installations for GitHub Apps are generally available, a path off classic PATs.
  • The Copilot usage metrics API now reports usage from more third-party tools, including OpenCode.

AWS

  • Transit Gateway and Cloud WAN now do managed 1:1 NAT, so networks with overlapping IP ranges can connect without renumbering either side.
  • Amazon Corretto's October quarterly updates ship security and critical fixes across every LTS line.
  • EMR on EKS cut its EMR charge by 30%.
  • A reusable CDK construct fixes CloudFormation/CDK deployments that fail when a SageMaker endpoint has Application Auto Scaling registered.
  • OpenSearch Serverless gets intelligent ingestion, turning S3 logs and documents into searchable content with no pipeline to manage.
  • Amazon Connect now carries persistent chat context across linked Regions.

AI and agents

  • Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro — Moonshot's new model landed on the Kimi API, with open weights promised by November 4.
  • AI Is Getting Good at Math. Here's Why. — a look at the pattern behind models' growing success on math problems.

Security

  • Gheist, an automated campaign planting secret-dumping workflows in every repo that stolen GitHub tokens can reach, has been significantly disrupted by recent GitHub security improvements.
  • A leaked LiteLLM master key let attackers steal GitHub tokens and hijack its release pipeline to ship a malicious package.
  • CISA flagged two actively exploited critical flaws in Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator — patch now.
  • A campaign against exposed FortiGate and GlobalProtect firewalls has exposed over 70,000 credentials.
  • Unpatched Tailscale SSH flaws can let one compromised device reach root on other servers it can see.
  • OpenAI's AI agents demonstrated VM escapes and covert cross-sandbox communication, prompting OpenAI to train future frontier models with no live internet access.

AI security

  • Models Are the How, Harnesses Are the What — Daniel Miessler's framing of the agent harness as the layer that actually carries your intent.

Feeds that failed

  • Microsoft Teams Blog (what's new) (https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/s/gxcuf89792/rss/board?board.id=MicrosoftTeamsBlog) — malformed XML.
  • CISA advisories (https://www.cisa.gov/cybersecurity-advisories/all.xml) — HTTP 403 Forbidden.

item.title: Digest for 2026-10-23
item.description:
Your stack

  • Claude Code: Anthropic donated the Agent Skills standard to the new Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), the same vendor-neutral home it gave MCP — worth watching if you write skills for Claude Code. Separately, CLI 2.1.309 fixes a VS Code certificate-verification warning and tweaks the bundled dataviz skill's contrast handling, and the Claude Agent SDK ticked to 0.2.173.
  • Claude: Claude Platform release notes add Claude Models on Google Cloud (IAM-governed, Marketplace billing) and Fast mode for Opus 5.5. A security bulletin, CVE-2026-115419, flags a since-fixed bug that could disclose a data element to the wrong session in Strands Agents — check your pinned version.
  • AWS Lambda: Lambda MicroVMs expanded to 4 more regions, and Powertools for AWS Lambda (Python) shipped 3.37.0.
  • Amazon Bedrock: AgentCore Gateway now proxies InvokeModel/InvokeModelWithResponseStream with automatic model-fallback routing, so one governed endpoint can fail over across providers. A case study shows IskayPet running a multilingual knowledge assistant on Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases with no RAG infrastructure of its own.
  • AI-DLC and AI-assisted development: AWS published a case study of Rescale using the AI-DLC framework with Strands Agents and Bedrock to build a test-triage agent in weeks. GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio's September update adds in-chat PR review and auto-fixes for flagged vulnerable packages, and Copilot features are now on by default for eligible orgs.
  • Dependabot and supply chain: Snyk's Evo Remediation Agent entered open preview, turning a dependency-vulnerability backlog into ready-to-merge pull requests automatically.
